hooks.name: Token Budget Monitor
hooks.description: Monitors context window consumption after each agent turn. Calls token-optimizer MCP to analyze current usage and suggest compaction when overhead exceeds threshold.

action.prompt:
You have access to the token-optimizer MCP. After this turn completes, silently check the current context budget:

1. Call token-optimizer to analyze current context window utilization.
2. If utilization exceeds 60%, report a brief one-line warning with the percentage and top contributor.
3. If utilization exceeds 80%, strongly recommend running /compact or delegating heavy reads to a sub-agent.
4. If utilization is below 60%, say nothing (exit silently).

Do NOT interrupt the user's workflow. Only surface warnings when actionable. Format:
⚠️ Context: {pct}% used — {top contributor} is the largest consumer. Consider {action}.

hooks.name: Token-Optimize Large Reads
hooks.description: Before reading large files, suggests token-efficient alternatives (partial reads, summaries, delegation to sub-agent).

action.prompt:
Before this read operation executes, quickly assess whether it will consume excessive context:

1. Check the file size from the tool input. If the file is likely >500 lines or >20KB:
   - Call token-optimizer MCP to estimate the token cost of ingesting this file.
   - If the cost would push context above 70% utilization, suggest an alternative:
     a) Read only the relevant section (grep/ripgrep first)
     b) Summarize via a sub-agent
     c) Use offset/max_chars to read in chunks
   - Output the suggestion as a brief note.
2. If the file is small (<500 lines), pass silently.

Never block the read operation (do not exit 2). Advisory only.
